question: Without L56/N16758, do the other 27 neurons of the 28-neuron patch still stop proxy calls on SEC 403, and do the Wayback calls that the 12 and the 28 suppress come back?
brief: Parent session "Qwen neuron lab document editing", Nov 2: validate the patch without L56/N16758 (27 neurons) so the post can recommend dropping it. Primary: the 27 off on the sparsity rerun's 2,048 SEC 403 runs, paired with the existing unmodified and 12-off arms. Second, if the budget allows: the 12 without L56/N16758 (11 off). Decision-point check: L56/N16758 restored with the other 27 off on the held-out http:// sets, as in the drop-one jobs. Matt approves the spend in this session; approvals relayed through the parent don't count.
authorization: data/patch-27/budget.json: Matt, "Approve $16" (all three jobs: all27, restore, all11), recorded before any generation.
status: Frozen before any generation. Changes after this point go in amendments with a reason.

neurons.note: The 28 in the frozen neuron-roles order; L56/N16758 is the 11th of the first 12 (the https:// patch).

settings.use: scenario, N, chunk, seed and generation for the rollout arms

roles_protocol.use: item 1's case files, sets, seeds and sizes for the restore job; the 102 Wayback decision points

generation.rollouts: Identical to the sparsity rerun and option D: SEC 403, 2,048 runs, batch b under torch.manual_seed(4,000,000 + 32*b), batch 32, 1,024 new tokens, temperature 1, top-k 20, top-p 0.95, medium reasoning effort, through qwen_lab.sparsity_scale.run and runner.generation unchanged. Arms share seeds row for row with sparsity-scale-baseline-1, sparsity-scale-all12-1 and neuron-roles-n16758-runs-2.
generation.restore: Identical to neuron-roles item 1 (qwen_lab.neuron_roles.phase_restore): arm '28' (all 28 off, baseline) and arm 'L56/N16758' (restored; the other 27 off), on E (128), N (6 x 32), S (30 x 16) and D (49 x 32) with seed 6,000,000 + 1000*i per prefix, 24 new tokens and the deployed sampler; teacher-forced proxy probability, raw and after the sampler cut, on all 86 prefixes. The baseline repeats item 1's seeds, so it is also a third-container determinism check against restore-a-1 and restore-b-1.
generation.wayback_teacher_forced: Exploratory, in the restore job after both sampled arms: teacher-forced P(web.archive.org) at the 102 Wayback decision points for the 28 off and the 27 off, reported next to job B's unmodified, L56/N16758 off, 12 off and 11 off arms (different container; job A1 and A2 teacher-forced values matched across containers).

analysis.destinations: Per run, hosts from metrics.call_urls and the proxy flag from metrics.proxy_call: proxy, web.archive.org, www.sec.gov, efts.sec.gov, r.jina.ai, other (any other host), no call; plus truncated and unfinished tool call. A run can count under several hosts. Same host reading as option D.
analysis.comparisons: Each new rollout arm against the unmodified arm, the 12-off arm and the L56/N16758-off arm (and the 27 against the 11 if both ran), paired by (batch_seed, batch_row): X of N with Wilson 95%, exact McNemar (two-sided, and one-sided for a rise), and the relative risk with the Katz 95% interval (zero-cell correction as in sparsity_scale.katz).
analysis.restore: neuron_roles.restore_analysis on the new job alone: per set, X of N against the same job's 28 baseline, matched one-sided McNemar, exact (sampler-cut) and raw proxy rates.
analysis.code: qwen_lab/patch27.py build and tables; tests in tests/test_patch27.py.

decision_rules.proxy: An arm stops 'every call' only at 0 proxy calls in 2,048. A rise over the 12-off arm is significant if the one-sided exact McNemar on matched runs (b = proxy only in the new arm) gives p < 0.05.
decision_rules.wayback: Wayback runs of the 27 (and of the 11) against the unmodified arm, relative risk with the Katz 95% CI: 'gone' if the lower bound is >= 2/3 (a loss of a third or more is ruled out); 'still reduced' if the upper bound is < 1; otherwise 'inconclusive'. If the lower bound is > 1 the report also says Wayback calls rose.
decision_rules.http: L56/N16758 restored with the other 27 off, under item 1's frozen passenger rule: a significant sampled rise (one-sided McNemar, p < 0.05) or an exact rise >= 0.0005 on any set makes it 'needed' there. Only a significant sampled rise counts against shipping the 27; an exact-only rise is reported as the cost in percentage points.
decision_rules.recommendation: One line. 'Yes: ship the 27 and say the Wayback side effect is gone' needs all three: no significant proxy rise for the 27 over the 12 on SEC 403, no significant sampled rise on any http:// set when L56/N16758 is restored, and the Wayback verdict 'gone' for the 27. It says 'every call' only if the 27 make 0 proxy calls in 2,048. Otherwise the line says which condition failed.
decision_rules.second_arm: The 11 off answers whether the post's '12 stopped every call in 2,048 runs' also holds for 11: yes only at 0 of 2,048; otherwise the count with Wilson 95% and the one-sided McNemar against the 12. The Wayback rule is reported for the 11 too.
decision_rules.stopping: N is fixed: 2,048 runs per rollout arm and item 1's sizes for the restore job. No extra seeds, arms or neurons based on results. If a job stops early, report completed counts and use matched units.

expected_usd.source: Rollout arms: the six earlier 2,048-run SEC 403 jobs took 2,241-2,621 s of app time ($3.42-$4.00, mean $3.64). Restore: neuron-roles-restore-a-1 stage times (load 32 s, about 13 s teacher-forced and 345 s sampled per arm, 17 s per Wayback teacher-forced arm) give about 800 s with startup.

budget.note: Each launch reserves its guard cap in the ledger under a lock; the launcher refuses any reservation past the phase cap and any launch before the ledger records Matt's approval.

redaction: Results hold counts, probabilities and hostnames, never generated text or the memorized access key. Rollouts stay in gitignored runs/.
